changes.current_line: Billing that helps you grow revenue.
changes.change: For buyers replacing a homegrown billing system, lead with roadmap capacity instead of revenue growth: "Change a price in minutes, not a quarter. Stop billing being a tax on your roadmap." When the champion reacts to the demo, use their framing back to them, as in "that's a quarter of roadmap in five minutes."
changes.why: Owen explicitly rejected the revenue framing ("we're not trying to grow revenue with billing, we're trying to stop it being a tax on the roadmap."), while the demo landed because he translated it into roadmap time.

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: Present the independent study only as a starting point. As soon as a champion asks for payback, offer a working session that week to build their own payback number with them: "The study shows what others saw. Let's build the number for your business, using your own costs, before it goes to finance."
changes.why: Owen asked "do you have something that shows payback?" and got the general study-based deck, then said "I can't get this past Diane without a number that's ours," and the session to build that number never happened before the freeze.

changes.change: Finance-facing cost-of-standing-still line for homegrown-billing prospects, filled in with the customer's own figures: "What your current billing costs you each quarter: engineering time on every pricing change, billing errors, and subscriptions that lapse when a card fails and nobody chases it." Pair this with a simple calculator. Bring in the M10 retry story here, as recovered revenue against their own lapse numbers.
changes.why: The missing proof was "Their own. What the homegrown system costs them," the inputs were named in the conversation ("some landlord subscriptions lapse because the card fails and nobody chases it. We never added it up."), and finance treated the deal as a nice to have because "if it isn't on fire, it isn't funded."

changes.change: Migration proof point for buyers replacing homegrown billing: a reference customer the prospect can speak to, one who moved existing subscriptions over in stages without asking their customers to re-enter card details. Offer this conversation alongside the migration doc, not instead of it.
changes.why: Owen asked about moving subscriptions "without asking landlords for their card details again, and whether they could do it in stages," and when offered a doc "He wanted to talk to someone who'd done it."
